Work: the Ministry of Employment and Human Resources' own summary of the Employment and Industrial Relations Code 2015 (minimum age): an employer shall not employ or engage a child under fifteen in any capacity except light work; children of thirteen or fourteen may do light work and are barred from hazardous work; a child labour regulation adopted in 2025 elaborates light and hazardous work (not read). The ILO's Child Labour Observatory profile for Kiribati adds that section 115(2) of the Code first allowed employment from fourteen and that a 2021 amendment raised the general minimum age, apprenticeships included, to fifteen. Performers: neither source names an exception or permit for performing, so barred under fifteen (my reading), save light work from thirteen, which the form doesn't hold. The Code's own text wasn't read. Service: Kiribati keeps no armed forces; no law on a call-up was read; null.

sources.title: Ministry of Employment and Human Resources (Kiribati): Employment and Industrial Relations Code 2015, page 2 (Minimum Age)
sources.said: An employer shall not employ or engage a child under 15 years to perform work in any capacity, except in light work. Children aged 13 or 14 may be employed in light work and prohibited from hazardous work.

sources.title: ILO Child Labour Observatory: Country profile Kiribati
sources.said: following its amendment in 2021, the general minimum age for employment—including apprenticeships—was raised to 15 years.
